en: Preface to the *Collected Praises for the Master of the Southern Mountain*, composed by the Śramaṇa of Yuhang, Shi Yuanzhao.
The magnificent achievements and noble deeds of our ancestral Sage-Master are fully recorded in Li Yong’s *Biography* and Yan Yuan’s *Original Stele Inscription*. Great...
The *Song Gaoseng Zhuan* (Biographies of Eminent Monks of the Song Dynasty) has been widely adopted by later worthies for the purpose of composing eulogies and hymns.

Whenever memorial services for the anniversaries of their passing are held, extensive offerings are presented; these are chanted and recited to express one’s sincere devotion and grief—a tradition that has long existed.
Formerly, Master Gushan was the first to take up the pen, doing so at the request of Doushuai Zewu Lushi. Subsequently, Master Xixi lamented its...
The ritual procedures were still lacking in melodic intonation and remained somewhat inconvenient; subsequently, another version was composed.

Vinaya Master Zhenwu of Tiantai employed both versions concurrently, feeling that singing alone was insufficient and thus further applying musical ornamentation to simulate the three-day period, alternating them in sequence.

Consequently, three versions circulated in the world, which may be said to be like gold and jade vying for brilliance, or orchids and chrysanthemums each claiming their own beauty. In later generations...
Although there were authors, their talent, insight, and literary skill were insufficient to rank alongside [the masters]; therefore, they have not been included.
Nevertheless, based on various biographies and records, I have examined the merits and defects of these works.

Wherever the phrasing or reasoning was unstable, or where the ritual protocols were deficient, I have made revisions throughout, so that later students may not be confused by divergent paths. Let us reflect upon this: the Buddha’s transformation has spread to the East.
Those who extensively propagated [the teachings] were quite numerous; though their conduct and deeds were renowned, even a single passage or a single hymn was sufficient to praise them.
Yet, as for our Patriarch alone, those who have offered hymns and eulogies number nearly several schools, yet they have ultimately been unable to exhaust his excellence.

This serves to demonstrate that his realization of the Way was lofty and profound, his merit deep and his practice subtle, beyond the reach of ordinary thought and deliberation. Fellow students of the same school, [you should know this].

If even those who [claim to be disciples] cannot receive instruction and cultivate their persons, how could they possibly contemplate virtue or honor the distant ancestors? This is the preface to the *Litanon for the Patriarchs of Nanshan*,
written on the anniversary of the Patriarch’s death in the third year of the Yuánfú era.
Narrated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhiyuan of Gushan.
I humbly observe that Zi-chan’s legacy of benevolence was praised by Confucius, and the ear-trees of Lord Shao were celebrated in the odes of the poets.
How much more so for the Great Master Chengzhao, the Teacher of the Southern Mountain, whose establishment of deeds and words has extensively expounded the study of the Vinaya without partiality.
Without faction, I reverently practice the school of the Dharma and Esoteric Teachings. Indeed, by distancing oneself from transgressions, one achieves observance;

by following from the state of an ordinary being, one enters the rank of the sages. This has given birth to my life of wisdom and nurtured my Dharma-body; such is the boundless debt of gratitude. How could I ever abandon the path of your contemplation?

Now, as I approach the anniversary of your passing, I look back with longing upon your compassionate influence. In establishing my character and spreading my reputation, I am ashamed to lack the excellence of the ancient worthies. May I be cautious in concluding my life’s end...
In commemorating those long departed, I hope to share the heart of a filial son. Thus, I have briefly displayed incense and flowers, and offered a simple presentation of pondweed and algae.

The receiving of blessings is not equal to the *yue* sacrifice, yet the offering to the spirits is truly akin to the waters of a marsh. Nevertheless, I have ventured to compose these crude words to sing of his enduring legacy.
Though the "hundred beasts dancing in unison" may serve as a metaphor for my humble person, how could I ever fully sing the praises of such magnificent virtue? May it suffice.
With eyes of compassion, secretly illuminating the minds of others, you have descended to this place of practice to accept these offerings.
With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite the Great Master Chengzhao, the Founder of the Nanshan School.
I only pray that you will descend upon this site of practice to accept my offerings. (Having made the request three times, they praise him in unison; the same applies below.

You act as a representative for those who have awakened, serving as an envoy of the Tathāgata. Dragons and māras submit to you, and mountain deities serve you. Your fame spreads throughout the five regions.
His words startle the ten thousand ages. The golden sun sinks in the west; the Buddha-sun rises in the east. With bowed heads we take refuge in the Patriarch who founded the Vinaya school.
(At this point, one may either provide a narrative or read the commentary, addressing the Patriarch by name; the same applies below.)

With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Venerable Master of the Southern Mountain, who manifested his spiritual form in the imperial capital in response to the needs of the age. (All subsequent entries shall follow this pattern.
The bright moon pierced his heart, manifesting auspicious dreams; He was born in China as a child of extraordinary character.
Though he possessed a sharp intelligence while dwelling in a family of accumulated merit, His profound clarity led him to a latent realization of the principle of non-arising.
He thoroughly understands the subtle tones of the Six Classics, reaching far and wide; he is profoundly versed in the Tripitaka, his internal realization deep and sublime.
How wonderful! To those who should appear in the form of a Vinaya Master, he manifests as a Vinaya Master to expound the Vinaya.
Therefore, with a single mind, I take refuge in and pay homage to him (the following sections are to be modeled after this).
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the one whose vast compassion transcends all models, who retired to seclusion to compose his commentaries;
Who dwelt in reclusion at Zhongnan, upholding the Vinaya-piṭaka; Whose pruning of redundancies and supplementation of omissions set him apart from other schools;
Whose magnificent prose rivals the brilliant morning clouds, And whose profound meanings shine as brightly as the autumn moon.
The five vehicles follow its guidance upon the level path; the Three Jewels, like a ship, encounter a swift wind.
To uphold the texts and practice the rites is not to rely on the void; through successive dynasties it has been revered as a great instruction.

With single-minded devotion, they prostrate themselves, their voices resounding throughout the Middle Kingdom and the surrounding lands, as kings and ministers reverently honor this temporal embodiment.
Upholding his reputation, he transmitted [the Dharma] to India; his pure and lofty virtue moved the Purple Palace and the Earth.
Master Xuanzang traveled west and was summoned to translate the scriptures; Master Amoghavajra came from the East and wished to rely upon him.
A portrait was painted during the Xianqing era to manifest his illustrious legacy; he was posthumously honored with a title during the Xiantong era to stir the dust of later generations.
The Emperor revered the teachers from foreign lands, and the world turned toward benevolence;
truly rare indeed was this one who, with single-minded devotion, prostrated himself before the image to uphold the teachings and recompile the History of the Sangha during his lifetime.
Grasping the brush and dipping the pen, he compiled and linked together the records of the most profound merits of eminent monks;
through refined diction and comparative analysis, he chronicled the multitude of worthies, censuring evil and encouraging goodness to bequeath his legacy to future generations.
All monastics revere his pen like that of Sima Qian, and all great scholars look up to his talent as that of Dong Gu.
May future generations, upon reading this, strive for complete emulation; may they ensure that the true Dharma wind does not fall to the ground.
With single-minded devotion, they pay homage and vow to advance in their practice, constantly abiding in meditative concentration at all times.
Diligently practicing the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, He dwells in the depths of a secluded, ancient temple.
For ninety days he exerts himself, stilling all external conditions; The myriad realms dissolve away, returning to the single thought-moment.
In the clear weather, the sound of the bell echoes through distant valleys; Ash falls from the incense burner as the lamp burns through the rain-soaked autumn night.
The multitude of dragons paid their respects by transforming into human form; they reformed their evils and mended their hearts, all withdrawing their venom.
With single-minded devotion, they prostrated themselves, as gods and humans alike turned to him for refuge. His profound spirit manifested auspicious omens, appearing at times in a physical body.
Retreating to seclusion at Qindu, Tiantong served him; Practicing the Way at Ximing, the Crown Prince followed him.
The Vinaya’s form was mysteriously identical to that of the Sage; The Buddha’s tooth was secretly bestowed by Nāṭa.
White springs overflowed as divine beings pointed the way; In imitation of his palm, the secluded wild beasts became docile.
Such a marvelous and rare wonder as this, its majestic virtue towering like the sun and moon—
single-mindedly I prostrate to the one who, at the foundation of his path, chose a superior site to build an altar and received the temporal body once more.
Manifesting the Buddha’s teachings surpassing all antiquity, A precious altar was thus erected within the Divine Land (China).
Majestic and five-tiered, it anchors the Golden Garden; Solemnly, the lords of the four quarters are arrayed as celestial rulers.
Its design accords with the rites of the Anāgāmins; Once its construction was completed, Pindola arrived.
Ascending to receive the precepts, the Dharma-body is perfected; now both assemblies have received this grace in full.
With single-minded prostrations, we repay your kindness as you have completed your earthly transformation and transferred your spirit to the Inner Court, where your temporal body remains.
The conditions of Jambudvīpa are nearing their end; the fruits of the palace of Cīna are about to ripen.
Heavenly beings first offered the fragrance of the thorn-forest; sitting peacefully, he soon reached his final end.
In the capital’s monasteries, empty flowers are neither real nor born from cessation; like the moon in water, he is without mind, letting go and coming as they may.
Responding to Maitreya, who succeeds Upāli, I pray to behold his descent to birth and discourse upon the Vinaya Piṭaka.
With a sincere heart, I repent (holding the incense burner, recite together with one voice while reflecting on transgressions;
the same applies below): Since beginningless kalpas, we have been deluded by the true purity, creating worldly toil.
Cycling through the various realms of existence, they receive subtle forms; Passing through many lifetimes, they undergo manifold sufferings.
The river of craving surges vast and wide, such that one forgets the way back home; In a decaying house ablaze with fire, they do not fear being consumed.
By chance, having attained a human body endowed with all faculties, They have gained entry into the Profound Gate to join the fivefold assembly.

Having shaved their hair and donned the dyed robes, they differ greatly from the worldly; yet though they ascend the altar to receive precepts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, within they lack lofty aspirations and long for transcendence.
Externally, they pursue the conditions of defilement, content with what is base and inferior;
their roots of goodness are meager and lost to circumstance, while evil habits entwine them, arising whenever they encounter objects.
The life-preserving bag is entirely lost as you block the long river; the axle of the chariot is shattered upon the perilous road.
How can such decayed and rotten things be worthy of the faithful offerings of the laity? This coarse negligence is utterly inconsistent with the true rule.
It is more than just a foolish monkey grasping at a tree branch; it exceeds even a thirsty deer rushing toward a mirage.
The nature of karma is like space, though it cannot be grasped; yet when the conditions for suffering converge, there is no deviation.
Once one loses this human body, it cannot be regained; sinking forever into other realms, by what means could one emerge?
Every time I contemplate birth and death, I harbor fear; thus I dare to pour out my very heart and soul to reveal everything.
Throughout all times in past kalpas and in this present life, I now face the Sage’s compassionate grace to repent of the boundless sins of the six sense organs and three karmas.
May these heavy natures and obstructive veils be instantly melted away like frost and snow;
Vowing to uphold them lightly, I look forward to awakening through profound dhyāna and wondrous wisdom.
Through diligent study of the three types of noble writings, I first came to know my return to the true path of the One Vehicle;
the story of abandoning one's body for a half-verse is heard, yet the debt of grace from a thousand lifetimes is difficult to repay.
With all my strength, I uphold the True Vehicle to illuminate the Buddha’s transformation, once again supporting the eternal norms and rectifying the monastic tradition.
Perfectly cultivating the three aggregates, I shall proceed toward Nirvana; Exhausting the four modes of birth, I shall lead all back to the blissful land of An-yang.
Even the great void may have its boundaries reached, But my vow shall never waver or shift.
I further pray for your protective mindfulness and secret empowerment, So that both my vows and my practice may be fully accomplished.
Having finished the repentance, one should single-mindedly take refuge and prostrate with the head.
This was originally composed by Master Gushan as a liturgy for inviting Arhats; it lacked verses of praise at the beginning and the repentance at the end consisted of only four lines.
Now, I shall append the true eulogy of Emperor Mu of the Tang Dynasty and my own verses of repentance and aspiration.
I have supplemented this, which possesses a certain degree of systematic order.

According to Li Yong’s *Biography*, the Buddha’s tooth was presented by the swift celestial deity, while Nanda merely attended upon him as an attendant. There are also other texts that refer to Nanda in this regard.
Therefore, let it remain as it is for now. Later, Zexi’s *Praise* also followed the old tradition; this was because he failed to examine the *Biographical Account*.
This is the *Text of Reverent Praise* by the Ancestral Master Nanshan.
